jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer
jobs.location: San Francisco Bay Area, CA, US
jobs.description: **About Arena Intelligence** ============================ Arena is the platform for evaluating how AI models perform in the real world. Founded by researchers from UC Berkeley's SkyLab, we're on a mission to measure and advance the frontier of AI for real\-world use, and to build the foundation for everyone to understand, shape, and benefit from it. Tens of millions of people use Arena each month to evaluate how frontier systems handle the work they actually do. The preferences they share power the most transparent, rigorous, and human\-centered evaluations in AI. Leading AI labs, enterprises, and independent researchers rely on our work and open datasets to understand how models behave in real workflows: agentic coding, creative generation, professional productivity, and beyond. We go beyond leaderboards and decompose what human experience reveals about AI, so models advance toward the work people actually do. We're a team of researchers, academics, builders, and creatives from UC Berkeley, Google, Stanford, and DeepMind. We seek truth, move fast, and value craftsmanship, curiosity, and impact over hierarchy. We're building a company where thoughtful, curious people from all backgrounds can do their best work together, in an office culture that radiates excellence, energy, and focus. ### **About the Role** This role has two core parts, both centered around working closely with the best AI labs in the world. First, you’ll partner directly with our lab customers to integrate their models, run and deliver evals, and act as their go\-to person at Arena Intelligence. You’ll plug into their research roadmap, understand where they’re headed, and help them get real value from our data. Along the way, you’ll spot gaps, surface new opportunities, and help shape what we build next. Second, you’ll roll up your sleeves and build. You’ll take on specific customer engineering asks and ship solutions that push the frontier of what our platform can do. Some of what you build may eventually scale into our Data or Applied ML stack — but it starts with solving real, high\-impact problems for cutting\-edge AI teams. ### **You’ll** * Own 5–15 active model lab relationships as the day\-to\-day point of contact * Partner directly with researchers and product teams to integrate models, run evals, and deliver high\-quality results * Drive consistent delivery across onboarding, data \+ product releases, co\-launches, and unblock unexpected issues fast * Be the “owner” of a key process improvement or automation (e.g., model onboarding flow, customer data insights, delivery tooling) * Translate customer feedback and research direction into concrete product ideas and engineering work * Work across the stack to ship pragmatic solutions that push the frontier for our customers * Help expand strategic accounts through trust, execution, and sharp technical judgment ### **You’ll have** * 4\+ years of software engineering experience with strong fundamentals (data structures, algorithms, system design) * Production experience in **TypeScript** and modern web frameworks * Hands\-on experience integrating LLM provider APIs, including streaming responses * Comfort moving across frontend and backend — you’re willing to dig in wherever the problem is * Familiarity with cloud infrastructure and CI/CD workflows * Strong problem\-solving instincts and the ability to operate in ambiguity * Clear, concise communication skills — you can explain complex technical ideas to both engineers and non\-technical stakeholders * A customer\-first mindset and a genuine desire to work closely with multiple stakeholders **What we offer** ================= * We offer competitive compensation and equity aligned to the markets where our team members are based. The base salary range will depend on the candidate’s permanent work location. * Comprehensive health and wellness benefits, including medical, dental, vision, and additional support programs. * The opportunity to work on cutting\-edge AI with a small, mission\-driven team * A culture that values transparency, trust, and community impact Come help build the space where anyone can explore and help shape the future of AI. Arena Intelligence *provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.* Compensation Range: $150K \- $250K

jobs.title: Controls & Embedded Systems Engineer - Field Deployment
jobs.description: **About American Turbines** The power grid was built for a world that no longer exists. Centralized generation, hundred\-mile transmission lines, decade\-long permitting cycles. Meanwhile, demand is exploding: AI data centers, industrial electrification, remote operations that need megawatts yesterday and can't wait for utilities to catch up. American Turbines is designing small modular gas turbines, purpose\-built for distributed power generation. Machines designed from a blank sheet to be manufactured at scale, clustered in arrays. Hundreds of units operating in parallel, dynamically matching load like a compute cluster matches demand. We are a seed\-stage company backed by the investors behind SpaceX, Boom Supersonic, and Hadrian. **About the Role** The Controls Engineer for our installation program will own running the microturbines we bring on\-site, first as a single unit and then as a fleet, on their existing controls. You are the person who gets these machines started, keeps them running, and relays every bit of turbine data back to HQ. You'll be based in San Francisco, but plan on stretches of weeks on\-site during installation and commissioning, not just the occasional trip. You will be on\-site for our first installation, working directly with the equipment rather than managing it remotely. You'll troubleshoot control issues in the field, in real time, on hardware we're still getting to know. Down the line, this work may also inform how we approach controls on our own turbines. This is not a desk job, but it's not permanent field presence either. You should want to be at a remote industrial site for weeks at a time when the work calls for it, hands\-on with the equipment, not just willing to tolerate it. **What We're Looking For** Experience with real\-time controls on complex, safety\-critical electromechanical systems, whatever the domain. Turbines, generators, industrial robotics, autonomous vehicles, anything where you had to get a physical system running and keep it running. What matters more than the specific system is that you get productive fast on unfamiliar hardware, reading schematics and control logic you didn't write and finding your way around them under pressure. You're the kind of engineer who wants to be at the site, not in the office reading the logs after the fact. You're comfortable being the person who has to figure out why something isn't working the way the manual says it should, on a system you didn't design. **Compensation** $165,000 to $215,000 base. Generous stock package. Medical, vision, and dental care. 2% matching on 401(k).

jobs.title: Controls & Embedded Systems Engineer - Prototype Development
jobs.description: **About American Turbines** The power grid was built for a world that no longer exists. Centralized generation, hundred\-mile transmission lines, decade\-long permitting cycles. Meanwhile, demand is exploding: AI data centers, industrial electrification, remote operations that need megawatts yesterday and can't wait for utilities to catch up. American Turbines is designing small modular gas turbines, purpose\-built for distributed power generation. Machines designed from a blank sheet to be manufactured at scale, clustered in arrays. Hundreds of units operating in parallel, dynamically matching load like a compute cluster matches demand. We are a seed\-stage company backed by the investors behind SpaceX, Boom Supersonic, and Hadrian. **About the Role** The Controls \& Embedded Systems Engineer will own getting American Turbines' first turbine to actually run: the embedded controls and firmware that take it from start to steady\-state operation, keep it running through every test, and shut it down safely when something goes wrong. This includes owning the P\&ID, sensor selection, and valve and plumbing choices, since those decisions are inseparable from what you're controlling, but the job is making the engine work. You will work directly with the test team to get the right sensors on the rig and define the control logic and firmware the engine actually runs on. As testing reveals what the engine needs versus what we assumed, you're the one closing that loop. This is not a role where controls comes in after the hardware is built. You will be embedded in the build from early on, shaping component choices around what's controllable and observable. **What We're Looking For** Experience with embedded controls and firmware for rotating machinery, engines, or similarly real\-time, safety\-critical systems. You've taken a system from a blank sheet to actually running, not just simulated or spec'd out. You think in failure modes and control loops as much as you think in code. You know how much of this job is judgment calls under uncertainty rather than clean spec work, and you'd rather be watching the engine run than writing the document that describes it. **Compensation** $175,000 to $225,000 base. Generous stock package. Medical, vision, and dental care. 2% matching on 401(k).

jobs.title: Data Analyst — DoT LiDAR
jobs.description: Precision Federal has been awarded a firm\-fixed\-price contract by the U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Highway Administration, to evaluate 3D LiDAR and smartphone\-based platforms for collecting motor vehicle traffic and roadway geometry data. The work is performed for the Turner\-Fairbank Highway Research Center. Purchase order 693JJ326P000024, awarded September 4, 2026, period of performance 24 months. Nine drivers will record a month of their daily trips on their own phones through two Iowa road sites, an innovative interchange and a winding two\-lane segment. A vehicle\-mounted 3D LiDAR survey covers the same roads. You are the person who makes sure the data that reaches the Government is complete, correct, and reproducible. What you would do \- Run quality checks on incoming trip data as it arrives: completeness, GPS and sensor sanity, timestamp continuity, coverage of each site per driver \- Keep the quality\-control log that goes to the Government with the dataset: what was checked, what was rejected, why \- Build the horizontal curve inventory for each site from the trip and LiDAR data: curve start and end points, radius, superelevation, and speed through each curve \- Compare posted speed limits against design\-supported safe speed at each curve, working with our licensed Professional Engineer who reviews the findings \- Produce the figures and tables for the Task 3 and Task 4 reports and the final report, reproducible from code \- Join a short progress call once a month Requirements \- Python with GeoPandas, Shapely, or GDAL, and SQL with PostGIS or an equivalent spatial database \- Experience checking real sensor or GPS data for quality: gaps, drift, outliers, clock offsets \- Comfortable computing geometry from coordinates: distances, headings, curve fitting, radius of curvature \- Reproducible work habits: scripts and notebooks under version control, results a second person can rerun \- Clear written English. Your QC notes go to a federal research center Preferred \- Transportation or roadway geometry work: AASHTO Green Book concepts, superelevation, design speed \- Experience with vehicle telematics, naturalistic driving data, or smartphone sensor logs (GPS, accelerometer, gyroscope) \- Point\-cloud experience: PDAL, Open3D, CloudCompare, or LiDAR\-derived surfaces \- Prior work on a federally funded research project, or a state department of transportation How this works Part\-time consulting on a funded federal contract, performed remotely on your own schedule. Roughly 80 to 150 hours between March 2027 and September 2028, concentrated in the collection month and the analysis and reporting periods. Hourly, invoiced monthly. You will be named on the project team and credited in the final report. Pay: $50\.00 per hour Application Question(s): * Describe one dataset where you found and fixed a quality problem in sensor or GPS data. What was wrong and how did you catch it? * Which of these have you used in the last two years: GeoPandas, GDAL, PostGIS, PDAL, QGIS, ArcGIS? * Have you computed curve radius or superelevation from coordinate or survey data? Where? * Are you willing to be named on the project team and credited in a report delivered to the Federal Highway Administration? Work Location: Remote

jobs.title: Engineering Manager
jobs.description: **YOUR ROLE** Engineering Managers work as part of a cross\-functional product team to build \& launch products that remove the friction from commercial insurance. You'll lead and manage a team of first class software developers that will rely on you to ensure their decisions and work have the full support of the company. Your team builds and operates AI\-enabled systems, including an agentic chat experience running against real submission and policy data. You'll own their quality, cost, and reliability in production. Your users will be small business owners who will use your work to understand, compare, and buy the commercial insurance their business needs. This is a self\-serve purchase experience, and conversion is the measure of whether it works. **WHAT YOU'LL DO** * Own what the team ships, including deciding what gets built when priorities are not handed down. * Be a hands\-on leader who can write \& test code, review features, and direct the technical activities for 4\-10 other engineers. * Operate with ambiguity. Requirements will be unclear and scope will change, and you'll make calls before all the data arrives. * Lead and participate in code and architecture reviews. * Own the agent in production: task completion, safe failure, escalation to a human, and cost and latency across the full multi\-call pipeline. * Set the autonomy boundaries. Decide what the agent does unattended and what requires a human in the loop, and be accountable for where you drew the line. * Ensure that teams are staffed to meet objectives; actively participate in the recruiting and onboarding of new engineers to meet growing demands. * Embody best practices and good work habits; mentor team members on engineering concepts such as unit testing, TDD, continuous integration, and linting. * Coordinate complex technical activities, define high\-level milestones, and track progress towards objectives in conjunction with Product Managers. * Mentor Tech Leads on your team and participate in the design and development of complex software, through all phases of the software development lifecycle. * Other duties and responsibilities as assigned. **YOUR LOCATION** This is a fully remote role, with the exception of onboarding and optional in\-office events. **Skills \& Experience** * A track record of shipping, with specific products you can point to and say you launched. * Comfort operating without close direction, including deciding what the team works on when priorities are not handed down. * Previous technical leadership or management experience in technology startups. * Experience shipping and operating LLM\-backed systems in production, not prototypes. * Experience with agentic systems in production, including multi\-step tool use, session state, and evaluating a pipeline rather than a single call. * Firm grasp of DevOps, Agile, CI/CD, code quality, and cloud architecture. * Proficiency in Ruby on Rails, Angular, or comparable, plus working familiarity with Python in an AI or data context. * The ability to straddle both high level milestones and low level technical details. * A strong desire to promote a healthy working environment. **NICE TO HAVE** * Experience with direct\-to\-consumer or e\-commerce products, including conversion funnels, checkout and payment flows, and experimentation. * Understanding of data governance, PII, and auditability constraints when regulated data flows through third\-party model providers. * Experience leading a team that uses AI coding tools, with a point of view on review standards. * Previous experience working in high\-growth tech startup companies. * Commercial insurance experience is a plus, not a requirement. **Physical Requirements** * Must be able to sit/stand/walk for prolonged periods of time (up to 8 hours per day), at a desk working on a computer. * Must be able to use standard office equipment for extended periods of time, including but not limited to, a mouse, keyboard, phone and video conferencing. Bold Penguin is the premier digital broker for commercial insurance. Their technology expands top\-of\-funnel demand and increases yield for enterprise partners. Through digital distribution, wholesale capabilities, and AI\-driven insights, they transform the lifecycle of both simple and complex risks, from prospecting to placement. **Benefits** We offer competitive compensation and progressive benefits that include: * Medical, Dental, and Vision * Flexible PTO Policy * 401(k) with a company match * Employee Assistance Program * Parental Leave * Disability and Life Benefits **Stay connected to the Glacier.** We have great SLACK channels for work and play. We also like to video conference and hold all\-hands "Waddles" regularly. **Penguin bling.** Like swag themed after a certain Antarctic bird? Just. You. Wait. Bold Penguin believes in inclusion. That’s why we’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer that considers all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. To learn more about our results\-focused culture and employee\-focused perks, read more on our **careers page**.

jobs.title: Expert Senior Software Engineer — AI Code Review
jobs.description: Expert Senior Software Engineer — AI Code Review is a remote engineering review track for evaluating production code, debugging traces, and developer\-facing AI outputs against real\-world correctness standards. Reviewers reproduce failures, write the unit test the model should have written, and explain the fix so the modeling team can target the gap. **Why this role matters** ------------------------- Engineering model quality lives or dies on whether the generated code actually compiles, passes tests, and handles edge cases. AuraOne pairs experienced engineers with the modeling team to grade outputs the way a code reviewer would. **Responsibilities** -------------------- * Run and reproduce candidate code outputs in a sandboxed environment for Expert Senior Software Engineer — AI Code Review assignments. * Grade senior swe engineering review solutions for correctness, style, and edge\-case handling. * Write minimal failing tests that demonstrate the bug a model output missed. * Compare paired solutions and rank them with a written rationale tied to the rubric. * Tag failure modes (compile error, runtime crash, off\-by\-one, security issue) with severity scores. * Document recurring code\-generation failures so the modeling team can target them. * Calibrate against gold\-standard reviews to keep inter\-rater agreement above target. **Qualifications** ------------------ * Strong day\-job engineering experience — you can read, run, and debug unfamiliar code for Expert Senior Software Engineer — AI Code Review work. * Comfort writing concise unit tests that capture a single failure mode. * Familiarity with a testing framework. pytest, Jest, or JUnit. Go test, RSpec, or whatever you use. * Clear written reasoning — your review note has to convince another senior engineer. * Reliable async availability for at least 10 hours per week. * Prior code\-review or technical\-interview\-grading experience is a plus. **Example tasks** ----------------- * Reproduce a generated engineering solution to a coding task, run the test suite, and grade it. * Write the smallest failing test that demonstrates a model's edge\-case bug. * Compare two paired solutions and rank them with a written rationale tied to the rubric. * Triage a security issue surfaced by a model and document the patch the model should have produced. **Nice to have** ---------------- * Open\-source contributions or a public portfolio that demonstrates production\-quality code. * Experience with the target language's standard tooling, linters, and idiomatic style guides. * Familiarity with security\-review checklists (OWASP, CWE) and AppSec patterns. **Skills** ---------- * Code review * Debugging * Unit testing * Software engineering judgment * Senior SWE engineering review **Work model** -------------- Remote — US\-eligible. Remote · Independent specialist contractor. Employment type: CONTRACTOR. Applicants must be authorized to work from US. **Compensation** ---------------- $150–$210 / hr **Application process** ----------------------- Apply through AuraOne's specialist intake for role\-specific routing and review. Final project scope, schedule, and contractor terms are confirmed before placement.

jobs.title: Field Engineer- Brownsville, TX

This role provides hands\-on experience supporting Project Managers and Superintendents while ensuring field work is performed according to plans, specifications, and quality standards. The position serves as a key link between the field and project team, with a strong emphasis on earthwork, utilities, documentation, and public agency compliance. This is a field\-focused role and an excellent opportunity for an early\-career professional looking to build a long\-term career in civil construction. **What You’ll Do** * Coordinate daily with Project Managers and Superintendents to support field operations and project execution. * Review and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and submittals to ensure compliance in the field. * Support field operations with layout verification, line and grade checks, and clarification of technical details. * Assist with coordination of earthwork, grading, underground utilities, drainage, and related infrastructure work. * Perform quantity take\-offs, track installed quantities, and support pay applications and cost tracking. * Coordinate materials testing activities. * Inspect materials and workmanship to verify compliance with contract requirements and quality standards. * Interface with field crews, subcontractors, inspectors, utility agencies, and project stakeholders. * Support safety compliance related to trenching, traffic control, and work around heavy equipment. * Maintain accurate daily reports, logs, and field documentation. * Identify field issues proactively and assist with resolution, including support for change order documentation. * Assist in in the preparation of workplans and JHAs. **What You Bring** * Working knowledge of heavy civil construction methods, materials, and field operations. * Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and public works standards. * Experience with construction project management software such as Procore or similar platforms. * Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast\-paced field environment. * Effective communication skills for coordinating with field personnel, subcontractors, and project teams. * Strong problem\-solving, analytical, and documentation abilities. * Proficiency with Microsoft Word and Excel. * Ability to adapt to changing field conditions and project needs. * Safety\-first mindset with a commitment to quality and compliance. **Education \| Experience** * Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Business Management, or a related field. * Approximately 1\-3 years of experience in heavy civil or infrastructure construction (internships or co\-ops accepted). * Experience managing RFIs, submittals, and drawings in Procore. * Exposure to geotechnical or construction materials testing. * Familiarity with public works standards (DOT, municipal, AASHTO, FHWA). * Field experience supporting earthwork, utilities, or site development projects.

jobs.title: Forward Developed Engineer
jobs.description: **Forward Deployed Engineer** **— Banking Platform** *Ship it, then go sit with the people using it. · Charlotte, NC* **Location** Charlotte, NC — on\-site at our headquarters, with travel to partner and client sites **Experience Required** 5\+ years building and shipping production software, including meaningful time in financial services and hands\-on experience building with Claude **Employment Type** Full\-time, exempt **Reports To** Technical Program Manager **Direct Reports** None. You work across engineering, product, operations, and directly with external partners. **Core Stack** React, Flutter, AWS, GitHub Actions, Claude (Claude Code and the Claude API) **Portfolio** Expected — see "Show Us Your Work" below **The Trade We're Offering** ============================ We're a smaller institution headquartered in a city full of very large ones, and we're not going to pretend we can match what the largest of them offer on every dimension. What we're offering instead is scope that those jobs structurally cannot give you. At a large bank, this work is split across four teams — a mobile team, a web team, a platform team, and a client\-facing integration group — and you'd own a lane in one of them. **Here, the whole path from commit to customer is yours.** You'll write the Flutter code, write the React code, own the pipeline that ships both, and then sit across the table from the people using what you built and watch where it breaks. Engineers who want that loop rarely get it at scale. If that's the job you've been trying to find, this is it.**About the Role** ================== We're hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer to build our banking platform and then take it into the field. This is a hybrid of product engineering and client\-facing solutions work: roughly two\-thirds building, one\-third embedded with the partners, vendors, and internal teams who depend on what you ship. The forward\-deployed part is the point. Most engineering organizations put layers between the person who writes the code and the person who has to live with it, and quality suffers in both directions. You'll close that gap. When an integration fails at a partner, you're the one who diagnoses it — not a support tier that escalates to a queue that eventually reaches engineering three days later. We also expect this person to be genuinely fluent with Claude — not as a novelty, but as core tooling. A small team competing against institutions a hundred times our size only works if each engineer's output is multiplied. You should already be building this way and be able to show us how. You'll work closely with the Senior Product Manager who owns the banking portfolio, and you'll have real influence over technical direction. We have opinions but not much legacy, which means your architectural decisions will still be standing in five years.**What You'll Own** =================== **Mobile Development — Flutter** -------------------------------- * Build and ship our customer\-facing mobile banking application in Flutter across iOS and Android. * Own the release process end to end — store submissions, staged rollouts, versioning, and the deprecation strategy for older clients. * Handle the parts of mobile banking that are genuinely hard: biometric authentication, secure local storage, session handling, offline states, and deep links from notifications. * Keep performance and app size honest on the low\-end devices real customers actually carry. **Web Development — React** --------------------------- * Build customer\-facing web banking experiences and the internal tooling our operations teams use daily. * Share logic and design language across web and mobile so the two products don't quietly diverge. * Build to accessibility standards — WCAG conformance is a regulatory expectation in consumer banking, not a nice\-to\-have. **Cloud Infrastructure — AWS** ------------------------------ * Design, deploy, and operate services on AWS — compute, storage, networking, secrets, and identity. * Own infrastructure as code so environments are reproducible and auditable rather than hand\-assembled. * Build for the availability and recovery expectations of a regulated financial institution, and be able to prove them to an examiner. * Watch the bill. Cloud cost discipline matters more at our size than it does at a bank that can absorb the waste. **Delivery Engineering — GitHub Actions** ----------------------------------------- * Own the CI/CD pipelines for web, mobile, and backend services. * Build automated testing, security scanning, dependency checks, and deployment gates into the pipeline. * Maintain the change controls and audit trail that a regulated environment requires — approvals, artifacts, and release evidence. * Make shipping boring. A deployment should be an ordinary Tuesday, not an event. **AI\-Assisted Engineering — Claude** ------------------------------------- * Use Claude Code as a daily part of how you build — across the codebase, in your at You Get Here** **What You Won't Get Here** The full path from commit to customer, owned by one person Anywhere to hide when something you shipped breaks Architectural decisions that will still be standing in five years A platform team that handles infrastructure so you don't have to Direct contact with the people using what you build Insulation from customers when a deploy goes badly Deploys in days, not release trains scheduled a quarter out A mature engineering organization with established process Genuine influence on technical direction from your first month Deep specialization — you'll work across mobile, web, cloud, and AI A mandate to define how a company uses AI, not to inherit someone's rules An existing AI platform team, or someone else's guardrails to inherit Budget for conferences, certifications, and continued learning A remote or fully flexible arrangement — this role is on\-site **Education** ============= * Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience. * **No degree requirement we'll hold rigidly.** Show us what you've shipped. Self\-taught engineers with production track records are welcome here. * AWS certifications are a plus and are not required. **Work Environment** ==================== On\-site at our Charlotte headquarters, Monday through Friday, standard business hours. Expect periodic travel to partner and client sites — typically a few days at a time, several times a year. Banking platform work occasionally means an evening or a weekend around a release, a core conversion, or an incident. We run a real on\-call rotation and we keep it humane.**Show Us Your Work** ===================== We ask candidates for this role to share code. A resume tells us where you've been; a repository tells us how you think. Send us **one or two repositories you've built** — ideally something involving Claude, a mobile or web application, or infrastructure you're proud of. Personal projects, open\-source contributions, and side work all count. **If your best work is proprietary, that is not a disqualifier.** Most engineers coming out of financial services cannot share what they built, and we're not going to penalize you for honoring an agreement you signed. In that case, tell us and we'll substitute a walkthrough conversation — you talk us through the architecture of something you built, the trade\-offs you made, and what you'd do differently. That serves the same purpose. What we're looking for either way: how you structure a project, how you handle the unglamorous parts, whether the README exists, and — where Claude is involved — what you chose to delegate to it and what you kept for yourself. We are not grading polish. A rough repository with clear thinking beats a tidy one with none. We will not ask you to complete an unpaid take\-home assignment. Your existing work, plus a conversation about it, is enough.**How to Apply** ================ Send a resume, links to your repositories (or a note that your work is proprietary), and a short note about something you shipped and then had to support in the field: what broke, what you learned from the people using it, and what you changed as a result. That story tells us more than a stack list does. If invited to initial screening, we'll ask you to share a portfolio or a few examples of your work so we can get a better understanding of your experience and creative approach. **Equal Employment Opportunity** ================================ *We are an equal opportunity employer committed to building a team that reflects the customers we serve. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. Reasonable accommodations are available at any stage of the hiring process — just ask.* Iw9E8gJI5Z

jobs.title: Founding Engineer, Applied AI
jobs.description: **About Parisi Labs** Parisi Labs is building foundational world models for physical industry. We are developing models that learn how complex physical systems behave and reuse that understanding across forecasts, scenarios, and operational decisions. Energy is our first proving ground. We combine historical and live data with operational context, bringing together machine learning research, data infrastructure, and software engineering to turn advances in modeling into useful technology for energy operators. We are a small technical team working directly with the founders on our core models, systems, and products. **About the role** We are looking for an engineer who can turn new modeling and agent ideas into working systems. You will build evaluations, data and inference workflows, backend services, internal tools, and product\-facing experiments while working directly with the founders and researchers. Your job is to shorten the path from hypothesis to reliable software and bring failures observed in real products and real data back into the next experiment. As the technology develops, you will help turn model outputs into useful forecasting, scenario\-exploration, and decision\-support capabilities. This is not a narrow ML infrastructure role, a pure research role, or a management job. You will own reusable technical capabilities, partnering with the data engineer on shared data foundations and the product engineer on the applications that expose those capabilities to users. **What you'll own** * Turn research and agent ideas into working prototypes, evaluations, internal tools, and customer\-ready capabilities. * Build reusable systems for forecasting, covariate search, model\-input preparation, inference, evaluation, and decision support. * Work across model code, APIs, data contracts, workflows, backend services, and lightweight product experiments. * Investigate failures in models, agents, and their surrounding systems, and turn findings into better evaluations and more dependable behavior. * Improve developer experience, observability, reliability, security, and deployment speed where they unlock more research and product progress. * Work with the CTO, Chief Scientist, and CEO on technical direction and the capabilities needed for customer deployments. * Help set the engineering standards for the team, including testing, technical documentation, and sound decisions about what to build or reuse. **What we're looking for** * A track record of taking ambiguous technical problems from an initial idea through implementation and reliable production use. * Strong software engineering skills across backend services, APIs, data workflows, testing, and debugging. * Hands\-on experience taking ML models or agent\-based systems into production, including evaluation, integration, failure analysis, and ongoing operation. * The ability to work in research and model code while also building maintainable services and developer tooling. * Technical judgment about when to experiment, when to invest in reusable infrastructure, and when a simpler solution is sufficient. * Clear communication and the ability to collaborate directly with researchers, product engineers, and founders. **First 90 days** * 30 days: Understand the modeling stack, data infrastructure, and how our technology is used in Ask The Grid; identify one high\-impact system to own. * 60 days: Ship a working capability that converts research, data, or customer learning into repeatable software. * 90 days: Own a durable technical capability and materially reduce repeated founder engineering work through reliable systems, tooling, or workflows. **Why join** You will help determine how the company's research becomes usable technology. The work spans experiments and production systems, with direct access to the people developing the models and the people using the resulting products. Your technical decisions will shape the engineering team we build around them. **Location and compensation** Location: New York City or Boston/Cambridge. This is a hybrid role — we expect in\-person collaboration 2–3 days per week. Salary range: $225,000–$280,000 USD.

jobs.title: Founding Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description: **About Sylvan** ================ Sylvan is building autonomous revenue teams. We help B2B companies grow and protect revenue from their existing customers by identifying revenue\-driving signals and deploying agents that act on them at the exact moment, across every account. We work with customers ranging from fast\-growth startups to Fortune 500 enterprises like ServiceNow. Our ambition is to power the top\-line of the economy. We are guided by a core principle: no assholes, high mutual respect. We operate at high intensity, but with deep respect. Direct, honest, and no egos — just a shared obsession to win. We’ve raised $10M\+ from world\-class investors and strategics including TQ Ventures and HubSpot Ventures. We are a fully in\-office company based in New York City. **We will only hire A\-players and are highly willing to go above\-market in ownership, equity, and cash compensation.** We want world\-class builders who are excited by the opportunity to be part of a category\-defining company at the earliest stage. It won’t be easy. We’re going to move fast. But, it’ll be fun. **The Role** ============ You own a customer from initial data access through a working, trusted system: understanding their business objectives, constructing the context layer our agents run on, building and deploying the workflows, enhancing the agent harness as you learn what breaks, and then proving the whole thing delivers customer outcomes. The hardest part up front is the data. Every warehouse is a mess in its own way: tables nobody documented, three competing definitions of ARR, and a data team with an hour a week to give you. Until that resolves into something clean and usable, nothing built on top is trustworthy. **What You’ll Do** ================== * Understand what the customer’s business objectives. Sit with the customer's revenue and ops leaders, get to the goals behind the request, and decide what is worth building against. * Onboard new customers end to end. Scope data access, explore the warehouse with no documentation, and map a chaotic schema onto real business concepts. * Stand up the ontology and verify the mapping. Interview the customer's data team and business owners, resolve their own inconsistent definitions, and validate the mapping before anything gets built on top of it. * Build the signals and workflows on top of it. The predictions and actions the customer actually sees, and the agent harness behind them. When a step produces bad output for one customer, you diagnose it and improve it. * Own the value case. Agree the success measure with the customer up front, then build the case that we delivered against it: the analysis, the evidence, the technical substance behind a story we can point to. You’re honest when the number didn't move, and specific about why. * Make the next deployment faster. Validation frameworks, eval harnesses, reusable mapping tools — what you learn at one customer ships as tooling rather than tribal knowledge. **What You’ll Bring** ===================== * You work at the frontier of agent\-driven development. You've built your own setup rather than living on the defaults, and you keep finding ways to get more out of agents than they give most people. * 3\+ years in a technical, customer\-facing role (forward deployed, solutions, or software engineering with heavy customer exposure); former founders strongly encouraged * Deep data warehouse fluency. SQL, dbt, and real comfort in an undocumented five\-year\-old schema with nobody left to ask. * You can sit with a customer's data or ops team, extract what a business concept actually means to them, resolve the cases where their own people disagree, and encode it. * Applied data science literacy. Distributions, seasonality, validation design, calibration. You know when a result is noise. * Painstaking through to the artifact. You'll chase a broken join for three hours because a number looked slightly off, and you'll care as much about whether the customer can actually interpret the output. Correct data in an unreadable form isn't delivered. * You define success metrics rather than report on them, and you can build the case that the work delivered. You can also tell a customer their number didn't move and why. * You hold a technical position under pushback from a customer or from us, and change your mind for evidence rather than authority. * High tolerance for ambiguity and unglamorous work. Based in NYC, excited to be in\-office. **Equal Opportunity** ===================== Sylvan is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities throughout the hiring process \- please let us know if you need any. Compensation Range: $180K \- $250K

jobs.title: Founding GTM
jobs.description: **About Proof of Human** ------------------------ Proof of Human is building the global standard for human verification across the internet. As the line between human and machine behavior becomes harder to discern, establishing who or what is behind every interaction is becoming foundational to the integrity of a digital world. Founded by Princeton PhD scientists, Mayank Agrawal and Matt Hardy, Proof of Human is a research and technology company developing the science, products, and infrastructure required to meet that challenge at global scale. As a public benefit corporation, we treat this work as both a technical frontier and a public responsibility, advancing the field while shaping the standards and governance for how human verification systems are developed, deployed, and used. **About the role** ------------------ We’re looking for a *Founding GTM* to join us to build the next phase of how Proof of Human goes to market. You’ll work directly with the founders and staff across sales, growth, and market development: generating pipeline, leading customer conversations, advancing deals, and turning both your intuition, your research, and what you learn on the front lines into sharper positioning, stronger systems, and clearer strategic direction. This is a deeply hands\-on role for someone who wants to create the playbook while running it. **What you’ll do:** ------------------- * **Market Development:** Test new industries, buyer personas, use cases, messages, and acquisition channels to determine where Proof of Human has the strongest opportunity to win. Use what you learn to recommend where the company and product should focus. * **Pipeline Generation:** Build targeted pipelines across our existing market and select new verticals through thoughtful outbound, warm introductions, events, partnerships, and other distribution channels you identify, to create a steady flow of growth opportunities. * **Customer Discovery:** Lead early conversations with prospective customers to understand their problems, priorities, urgency, decision process, and willingness to commit. Clearly communicate Proof of Human’s value to both business and technical stakeholders. * Deal Execution: Own opportunities from initial outreach through discovery, demos, pilots, pricing conversations, close and commercial follow\-up, working closely with the team to move qualified deals toward close while maintaining a consistent momentum throughout. * Sales Enablement: Create the materials that help deals move forward for you and the team, including tailored follow\-ups, pitch decks, business cases, pilot proposals, objection handling, case studies, and vertical\-specific narratives for the buyer and use case. * Growth Experimentation: Run lightweight, measurable experiments across audiences, messaging, distribution channels, and conversion points. Use the results to determine what should be scaled, changed, or stopped, and turn tests into repeatable programs . **You’ll be a good fit if:** ---------------------------- * **Nobody has to hand you a map.** There’s no established process yet for much of what this role touches. You find a starting point, try something, learn from the result, and build the next version without losing momentum as conditions change. * **You’re curious across disciplines**. Whether you’re speaking with an academic, engineer, or business executive, or entering an unfamiliar market, you want to understand the substance and communicate in the language of the person across from you. * **You move fast once you see what needs to happen.** You don’t wait for the perfect moment or someone’s blessing. You take ownership, bring other people along, and keep pushing through ambiguity, friction, and setbacks until the work is finished. * **You think in hypotheses**. You turn open\-ended questions into focused experiments, define what you need to learn, and pay attention to the evidence. When the answer changes, you adjust your approach without getting attached to the original idea.

jobs.title: Lead Engineer - Prototype Build
jobs.description: **About American Turbines** The power grid was built for a world that no longer exists. Centralized generation, hundred\-mile transmission lines, decade\-long permitting cycles. Meanwhile, demand is exploding: AI data centers, industrial electrification, remote operations that need megawatts yesterday and can't wait for utilities to catch up. American Turbines is designing small modular gas turbines, purpose\-built for distributed power generation. Machines designed from a blank sheet to be manufactured at scale, clustered in arrays. Hundreds of units operating in parallel, dynamically matching load like a compute cluster matches demand. We are a seed\-stage company backed by the investors behind SpaceX, Boom Supersonic, and Hadrian. **About the Role** The Lead Engineer will own the timeline for American Turbines' first turbine, from where it stands today through a fully built and tested demonstrator. You will turn a stack of engineering workstreams, combustion, aerodynamics, mechanical, controls, power electronics, into a single execution plan, and you will be the one accountable for whether that plan holds. You will set the schedule, break it into tasks, and delegate those tasks to the engineers who own them. You will run daily and weekly engineering meetings, track what's actually getting done against what was promised, and step in wherever the build needs another set of hands: fixturing a part, running a test, chasing a vendor. Beyond keeping the schedule honest, you'll pick up engineering work directly when the team needs it, whether that's helping debug a test rig issue, sanity\-checking a design call, or just taking a task yourself when someone's stuck. This is not a role where you set a plan on a whiteboard and let the team execute it on their own. You will be in the shop as often as you're in a planning meeting, and the team's respect for your leadership will come from both. **What We're Looking For** A track record of taking hardware from 0 to 1 and shipping it, ideally at a small, fast\-moving hardware team. You don't need direct turbomachinery experience. What you need is the judgment to build a realistic timeline, the discipline to hold a team to it, and the willingness to get your hands dirty when the schedule calls for it. You've led engineers more senior or more specialized than you before, and you know how to earn their trust rather than assume it. You default to build\-and\-test over simulation, and you know the difference between a schedule slip that's normal and one that's a real problem. You're effective at quick check\-ins, not just deep dives. You won't have time to go deep on every workstream, so you need to know when a two\-minute conversation is enough to unblock someone and when a problem actually needs you to sit down and work it with them. **Compensation** $200,000 to $250,000 base. Generous stock package. Medical, vision, and dental care. 2% matching on 401(k).

jobs.title: ML Data Platform Engineer
jobs.description: **About Parisi Labs** Parisi Labs is building foundational world models for physical industry. We are developing models that learn how complex physical systems behave and reuse that understanding across forecasts, scenarios, and operational decisions. Energy is our first proving ground. We combine historical and live data with operational context, bringing together machine learning research, data infrastructure, and software engineering to turn advances in modeling into useful technology for energy operators. We are a small technical team working directly with the founders on our core models, systems, and products. **About the role** We are looking for an ML Data Platform Engineer to make the data behind our models, products, and customer deployments dependable, understandable, and easy to use. This role sits where data engineering meets machine learning. You will turn messy, changing real\-world sources into durable datasets and interfaces that researchers and engineers can trust. Your work will support both public data and customer\-authorized operational data. The goal is not to build a large platform for its own sake. It is to make each new model, product capability, and data source faster to bring online without compromising correctness. You will own the shared data foundations, working with the applied\-AI engineer on model requirements and the product engineer on application needs. **What you'll own** * Build and improve ingestion, backfills, validation, and observability for high\-volume, time\-dependent data. * Define clear data contracts and point\-in\-time semantics for model training, evaluation, and product use. * Create reusable workflows for bringing public and customer\-authorized sources into the system. * Build quality, lineage, freshness, and access controls that make data trustworthy in repeated use. * Develop efficient datasets and query interfaces for machine\-learning and product workloads. * Diagnose whether failures originate in source data, transformations, model inputs, or serving systems. * Work with researchers and engineers to turn recurring data requirements into reliable software rather than manual projects. * Decide which abstractions should become shared infrastructure and which should remain purpose\-built. **What we're looking for** * A record of designing, building, and operating production data systems that researchers or engineers depend on. * Strong programming, querying, and data\-modeling skills, with the ability to write maintainable, tested production software. * An understanding of time\-dependent data correctness, including backfills, revisions, freshness, and point\-in\-time availability. * Experience supporting ML training and evaluation, or similarly demanding data\-intensive product workloads. * The ability to design practical data contracts, validation, observability, and access controls without overbuilding the platform. * Strong debugging and collaboration skills, including the ability to trace failures across systems and explain data limitations clearly. **First 90 days** * 30 days: Understand the data lifecycle behind Ask The Grid and our ML work, and identify the most consequential reliability and usability gaps. * 60 days: Ship a reusable ingestion, backfill, validation, or dataset capability used in active product or research work. * 90 days: Own a dependable end\-to\-end data workflow, with documented contracts, quality checks, and clear operational visibility. **Why join** The quality of our models and products depends on the quality of their underlying data. You will shape that foundation early, working directly with researchers and engineers who use it, and see your work support new experiments, product capabilities, and customer deployments. **Location and compensation** Location: New York City or Boston/Cambridge. This is a hybrid role — we expect in\-person collaboration 2–3 days per week. Salary range: $175,000–$245,000 USD.

jobs.description: **About American Turbines** The power grid was built for a world that no longer exists. Centralized generation, hundred\-mile transmission lines, decade\-long permitting cycles. American Turbines is designing small modular gas turbines, purpose\-built for distributed power generation. Machines designed from a blank sheet to be manufactured at scale, clustered in arrays. Hundreds of units operating in parallel, dynamically matching load like a compute cluster matches demand. Shaft speed on a machine like this is likely to vary with load, so expect to be designing for a moving target rather than a fixed input. You will design the power stage, select and procure the components, and get it running alongside a live turbine on the test rig, working through real constraints: thermal limits, fast load transients, and a system that has to hold up over hundreds of hours of testing, not just a bench demo. You'll also work closely with the Controls Engineer on the telemetry and sensing handoff between the power stage and the embedded controls. This is not a role where you design in isolation and hand off a board to someone else. You will be present for testing, watching your power electronics perform under real engine conditions, and iterating from what you see. **What We're Looking For** Experience designing power electronics for variable\-speed or high\-frequency rotating machinery, motor drives, or similarly demanding electromechanical systems. You're comfortable working when the electrical architecture isn't fully specified yet, and you can reason from first principles about tradeoffs like direct\-drive vs. geared, or motoring\-capable vs. separate starter, not just execute against a fixed spec. You understand the tradeoffs between efficiency, thermal margin, and component cost, and you can make a call under time pressure rather than waiting for a perfect answer. You've seen your own hardware fail during test and know how to debug it fast. **Compensation** $175,000 to $225,000 base. Generous stock package. Medical, vision, and dental care. 2% matching on 401(k).
